newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said as the head of the government she believes in and pursues the policy of democratic obligation, fraternity and accountability. "There should be transparency in the state decisions," she told a televised question-answer session on Tuesday marking the completion of her 100 days in power.
Maldives President Mamoon Abdul Gayoom is scheduled to pay a three-day official visit to Bangladesh from October 16, diplomatic sources said.
Malaysia would not deport Bangladeshi workers who are now staying there, said Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Abul Hasan Chowdhury on return from a visit to Kuala Lampur.
Bangladesh's frontier guards have launched a drive to remove land mines alongside the borders with Myanmar, beleived to be planted by Burmese troops.
Dhaka Stocks Exchange will open a new trading floor from November providing modern trading facilities.

About 3.5 million people were rendered homeless in Bangladesh due to river erosion between 1990 and 1994, a seminar was told. More than 0.5 million acres of cropland have also been devoured by eroding rivers during the period.
